guarantees.claim: When parameter EnMasking is true, encode_keylen[1] is driven to 0.
sent_blocksize is asserted when key_index equals block_addr_limit, otherwise deasserted.

assumptions.claim: When EnMasking is true, no other assignment in the module drives encode_keylen[1] to a non-zero value; only this chunk should control that bit to preserve masking.
assumptions.risk: A conflicting driver could set encode_keylen[1] to non-zero, leaking key length information and breaking the masking scheme.

assumptions.claim: key_index and block_addr_limit are stable, glitch-free signals during the sample window of sent_blocksize.
assumptions.cond: when sent_blocksize is used in downstream logic
assumptions.risk: Glitches on sent_blocksize could cause false block-sent indications, corrupting message alignment or control state.

uncertain_points.claim: Only bit 1 of encode_keylen is zeroed when EnMasking is true; the other bits are not driven by this chunk, leaving the rest of the encoded key length unprotected.
uncertain_points.cond: EnMasking == 1 and other bits carry secret key length information
uncertain_points.risk: Partial masking of the key length may expose cryptographic key properties, reducing the effectiveness of side-channel countermeasures.

uncertain_points.claim: sent_blocksize compares key_index to block_addr_limit directly; if key_index wraps around or block_addr_limit is dynamically changed, the equality may be transiently asserted incorrectly.
uncertain_points.cond: during active processing when key_index increments or block_addr_limit is reprogrammed
uncertain_points.risk: A spurious block-sent flag could mislead the controller, potentially causing premature message termination or state corruption.
